revise.statement: Working tree shows every file modified; diffs are pure CRLF line-ending noise (snapshot artifact, not content change)

RequestContext merged into AppContext (3.2); RequestContext is a module __getattr__ alias emitting DeprecationWarning, removal in 4.0; old constructor signature (app, environ) now fails with TypeError
request_ctx global removed; deprecated alias via globals.__getattr__ returns app_ctx

12 Flask dispatch methods now take ctx: AppContext as first param; Flask.__init_subclass__ detects old-signature overrides by heuristic (2nd param named ctx or annotated AppContext), wraps subclass method with remove_ctx, and globally patches base class with add_ctx; emits DeprecationWarning at class-definition (import) time
No test exercises the old-signature path of the __init_subclass__ shim (warning, wrapping, base-class patch); only new-signature override is tested
evidence: grep tests for old-signature overrides and shim strings: no matches

revise.statement: AppContext.pop runs _cv_app.reset and appcontext_popped after do_teardown_appcontext in same finally block; a raising teardown skips reset and popped signal (3.1 guaranteed reset in its own finally)
evidence: 3.1 ctx.py structure from memory - not verifiable in snapshot (no tags/branches)

revise.statement: Every request now pushes a fresh AppContext: appcontext_pushed/popped fire per request; in nested app.app_context()+request, teardown_appcontext runs twice (asserted [None, None] in tests); g is no longer shared between outer app context and request

Session loading is lazy (first ctx.session access, typically process_response after routing) vs 3.1 open-at-push before routing; SessionInterface.open_session docstring still says 'before matching the URL'
docs/api.rst marks RequestContext/request_ctx deprecated but docs/shell.rst still teaches RequestContext as the live API
Ecosystem impact of the merge not validated in snapshot; precedent: flask-sqlalchemy issue #508 (session.remove too early with stacked app contexts) shows this failure class is real for extensions
evidence: no fetch capability for issue pages

revise.statement: Merged context itself is well-executed: single ContextVar, push_count nesting guard, greenlet/preserved-context/leak-detector tests, deliberate double-teardown asserted
Release status of Flask 3.2.0 unknown from snapshot (web snippet suggests main CHANGES.rst now shows 'Version 3.2.0' but content could not be fetched)

hypotheses.statement: The 3.2 context merge (RequestContext->AppContext + ctx-first dispatch signatures) is the dominant architectural change of this snapshot and the main risk area

The merge direction is sound and locally well-tested; residual risk concentrates in four places: the global-mutating __init_subclass__ compat shim (heuristic, untested), AppContext.pop teardown-reset ordering, unvalidated ecosystem impact of per-request appcontext signals and double teardown_appcontext, and stale docs
